stimuli.title: Seven employees hold seven distinct ranks (rank 1 is junior-most and rank 7 is senior-most).
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. In the stated ordering, Uma comes before Esha, and Esha comes before Bharat.
2. Jai is at rank 7.
3. Anika is exactly 2 positions senior to Bharat.
4. Isha is exactly 3 positions senior to Varun.
stimuli.solution: rank 1: Uma; rank 2: Varun; rank 3: Esha; rank 4: Bharat; rank 5: Isha; rank 6: Anika; rank 7: Jai

stimuli.title: Seven contestants finish at different positions in a race (position 1 is last and position 7 is first).

stimuli.title: Seven people live on different floors of a seven-storey building. Floor 1 is the bottom floor, and floor 7 is the top floor.

stimuli.title: In a certain coded language, each word has one unique code.
stimuli.body:
breeze temple inland = po qa zu
inland yellow pearl = bi zu sa
breeze golden pearl = po xe bi
yellow temple golden = qa xe sa
stimuli.solution: inland=zu, breeze=po, temple=qa, pearl=bi, yellow=sa, golden=xe

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain X < V > W ≤ R = T, decide which conclusions follow. I: X > T. II: V > T.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain X = T > R > S ≤ P, decide which conclusions follow. I: X ≥ R. II: X ≤ T.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain V > R > S ≥ Z < P, decide which conclusions follow. I: V ≥ S. II: R ≥ P.

questions.stem: Statements: Some farmers are readers. Some readers are poets. Conclusions: I. Some farmers are poets. II. All poets are farmers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The specified intersections do not force A and C to overlap or include one another.

questions.stem: Statements: Some bakers are dancers. All dancers are poets. Conclusions: I. Some bakers are poets. II. All bakers are poets. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Some A–B members must be C; not all A need be C.

questions.stem: Statements: No coders are runners. Some runners are sailors. Conclusions: I. Some sailors are not coders. II. No sailors are coders. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The B∩C members are outside A; other C members remain unrestricted.

questions.stem: Statements: All workers are poets. No poets are readers. Conclusions: I. No workers are readers. II. Some workers are readers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: A is contained in B, while B and C are disjoint.

questions.stem: Statements: Some readers are farmers. No farmers are painters. Conclusions: I. Some readers are not painters. II. All readers are painters. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The A∩B members cannot be C.
